title: We Have Thought on Your Steadfast Love
summary: If we don't stop and think on the Lord, we can hit the gas on the day and never notice what we missed. Count his mercies, and you will praise him.
exhortation: What struck me in these verses is that God's presence always brings joy, rejoicing and wonder. When we pause to ponder the Almighty and give thought to all his wondrous ways, we can't keep silent about it. It will affect us.

But if we don't stop "in the midst of your temple," we may miss it. We can easily hit the gas on the day and the tasks that have to get done and never think twice, without even realizing anything was missed. We give our time and thought to a thousand tasks and chattering nothings that seem so significant in the moment but leave us one day older and our souls a little thinner.

So have you stopped in your fast-paced days, yesterday and the day before, to think on the Lord? Have you meditated on his goodness and considered his steadfast love? Think of every time you needed the steadfast love of the Lord in your life. It was there for you. It doesn't waver when you prove faithless, unsteady or unworthy. It's right where you left it, steadfast and sure. Count his mercies toward you. Remember each one specifically and bring them to the front of your mind, and you will praise the Lord.

"As your name, O God, so your praise reaches to the ends of the earth." His name, his fame and the rumor of his greatness stretch throughout the land. "Your right hand is filled with righteousness." In a world full of darkness, trouble and evil, he reigns in truth. So, Christian, rejoice. Sons and daughters of the King, testify this morning to the mercy and grace poured out on you. Think on his steadfast love in your life, and rejoice.
prayer: Lord, like Isaiah, when we see your glory we say, "Woe is me, for I am a sinful man." It is a fearful thing to be in your presence. And yet, by your grace, we are not destroyed but lifted up, cleansed, restored, made righteous, filled with power and strength through your Holy Spirit, and called to sing grateful songs of praise for your grace, mercy and steadfast love. What an amazing thing it is to relate to you and not be consumed.
Open our eyes to your glory, to the wonder of your presence, and to the cleansing that comes from your blood, by which the unclean are made clean and can come into your presence. Thank you, Lord.
